title: Client disconnect lease revocation and partial-draft reconciliation
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Problem: When clients disconnect mid-generation (network blips, app backgrounding, or SDK crashes) we currently leave partial generations, leased KV cache entries, and in-flight function/tool-call state in the runtime for a long TTL. This increases memory pressure, leads to stale partial outputs being visible to resumed sessions, and complicates billing/telemetry. Goal: introduce a lease revocation + partial-draft reconciliation protocol that lets the runtime reclaim resources predictably while enabling safe resume paths for supported SDKs and graceful abort for incompatible clients.
background: We already have heuristics that GC ephemeral outputs after TTL and tombstone stalled sessions, but customers report resource spikes in high-concurrency workloads and flaky SDKs cause many orphaned prefixes. The design must balance safety (not losing final user-visible generations) with cost and operational simplicity. Must be compatible with function/tool-calling and structured outputs so partially executed tool calls are not double-invoked on resume.
acceptance_criteria: Lease record per streaming session with owner client token and epoch; runtime can mark leases revoked and expose reason codes
KV/prefix cache entries tied to lease epoch and eligible for reclamation after revocation grace window
SDK handshake changes: resume token includes last successful function-call boundary and checkpointed KV snapshot id
Runtime prevents double tool invocation when resuming; tool calls in partially-executed state are either completed atomically or rolled back via idempotency token
Metrics: orphaned-session-count, reclaimed-prefixes, avg-time-to-reclaim, and percent-resumes-without-dup-tool-calls
End-to-end e2e tests covering abrupt disconnect, reconnect within grace period (resume), reconnect after reclamation (new generation), and SDKs that do not support resume (abort)
Rollout plan with feature flag gated on SDK version and per-tenant toggle; no customer-visible errors by default
implementation_notes: Key pieces: 1) Per-session lease record in the allocator with fields: client_token, epoch, last_activity_ts, grace_window_ms, suspended_tool_state_id. 2) On unexpected disconnect, mark lease revoked and start reclaim timers. 3) Expose lease state via telemetry endpoint and add admin endpoint to forcibly reclaim. 4) SDK handshake: when resuming include resume_token {lease_epoch, kv_snapshot_id, last_function_call_id}. 5) On resume: runtime verifies lease_epoch matches or was revoked within grace_window and either rebinds existing KV snapshot or creates new generation. 6) Tool calls must be guarded by idempotency IDs and runtime-side dedup table keyed by function_call_id + attempt_number.
tradeoffs: Short grace windows reduce memory overhead but increase chance of losing ability to resume for mobile apps that background for long periods. Long grace windows preserve resume semantics but increase pressure on the KV cache. We opt for a 30s default grace window with per-tenant override and SDK-level opt-in for extended resume (up to 5m). Implementing idempotency for function calls adds storage overhead in the dedup table; we store entries with TTL equal to the longest resume window to bound costs.
progress_updates: 2026-02-20: Ticket created. Initial problem framing and acceptance criteria drafted (Ava).
2026-02-23: Spike completed: measured orphaned prefix growth under high-concurrency replay workload; avg orphan TTL observed 14m increasing memory by ~12% (Rohan). Findings linked in design doc.
2026-02-27: Design review with runtime and SDK teams. Decided on lease epoch model + resume token extension. Action: runtime implement lease records; SDKs add resume_token support (Rohan, Priya).
2026-03-01: Runtime prototype push: lease record and reclaim timer wired; basic admin reclaim endpoint added. Instrumentation emits orphaned_session_count metric (PR #6123).
2026-03-05: SDK JS PR adds resume_token parsing and resume handshake. Need integration tests to validate function-call dedup across reconnects (blocked on ENG-389001 dependency).
testing_plan: Unit tests for lease state transitions, integration tests that simulate flaky client disconnects with function calls in-flight, and chaos tests that kill SDK process after different boundaries. Add a load test with 10k concurrent streams to validate memory reduction after reclamation. Test matrix includes: resume within grace window (expect same generation), resume after reclaim (expect new generation and metrics emitting 'resumed_after_reclaim'), and incompatible SDK behavior (expect abort with 'client_unsupported_resume' event).
rollout_plan: Phase 1: internal canary in staging for 48h with feature flag on. Phase 2: limited tenant opt-in by SDK version for 2 weeks. Phase 3: global rollout with per-tenant config and console toggle. Monitor orphaned_session_count, reclaimed_prefixes, error_rate, and percent-successful-resumes. Have rollback plan to disable lease revocation if regressions > P0 thresholds.
